name: Project Scaffolding
one_line_goal: Stand up a buildable, lint-clean Flutter skeleton whose folder structure and stub screens exactly match the approved design.
objective: Set up the Flutter project structure, dependencies, tooling and navigation shell without implementing any business logic or persistence.
rationale: A scaffold that matches the architecture document is a cheap contract check. If the tree cannot be built as designed, the design was wrong, and finding that out now costs an hour instead of a refactor.
entry_criteria: ARCHITECTURE.md approved, including the directory tree and technology decisions.
NAVIGATION.md approved, including the screen inventory.
Flutter SDK installed and flutter doctor reports no blocking Android issues.

traceability.supports: All later stages; this stage produces no user-facing behaviour of its own.

how_to_work_this_stage.unit_of_work: One substage per working session. Work them strictly in listed order; do not parallelise or skip.
how_to_work_this_stage.between_substages: Tick the substage off, append evidence to docs/reports/STAGE_3_WORKLOG.md, then start the next. No user approval needed between substages.
how_to_work_this_stage.at_stage_end: The final substage assembles the stage report and stops for user approval before the next stage file is opened.
substage_list: 3.3 Dependencies and the code generation toolchain
3.4 Linting, formatting and invariant guard checks
3.6 Theme, design tokens and the money formatter

substages.name: Project initialisation and Android configuration
substages.goal: Create the Flutter project with final identifiers and correct SDK levels, and prove it builds and launches.
substages.why_it_matters: The application id can never change after the first Play Store upload, and SDK levels chosen carelessly become plugin conflicts later.
entry_criteria: ARCHITECTURE.md approved, including the directory tree and technology decisions.
NAVIGATION.md approved, including the screen inventory.
Flutter SDK installed and flutter doctor reports no blocking Android issues.

work.action: Choose the application id and treat it as permanent.
details: Reverse-domain form, based on a domain you actually control.
State it in docs/ENVIRONMENT.md and note that it is immutable after first upload.
Confirm it with the user if there is any doubt - this is cheap now and impossible later.

work.action: Create the project targeting Android only, and delete every trace of the counter template.
details: No template widget, no template test, no template comment survives this substage.

work.action: Set minSdk provisionally, and record that it will be re-checked in substage 3.3 once plugins are added.
details: Do not guess a number from memory; start from the Flutter SDK's current floor and raise only if a plugin demands it.
Record which plugin sets the floor once known.

work.action: Set compileSdk and targetSdk to the levels currently required by Play policy.
details: Check the current requirement in official documentation rather than relying on remembered numbers; the required level rises annually.

work.action: Configure Gradle, Kotlin and Java versions consistent with the Flutter version in use, and resolve any warnings rather than suppressing them.
Configure the Android manifest minimally.
details: Application label, no unnecessary permissions, no cleartext traffic, no backup rules left to default - note that backup configuration is decided deliberately in Stage 9.

work.action: Build and launch on a physical device or emulator, and capture the command output verbatim for the stage report.
Write docs/ENVIRONMENT.md.
details: Flutter version, Dart version, Gradle, Kotlin, Java, minSdk, targetSdk, compileSdk, the reason for the minSdk floor, and the exact build commands.

acceptance_criteria: flutter build apk --debug succeeds with no warnings referencing the template.
The app installs and launches to its own first screen, not the Flutter demo.
docs/ENVIRONMENT.md records every version and the minSdk justification.
The application id is final and recorded.
must_not: Do not leave template code in the repository.
Do not suppress a Gradle warning rather than resolving it.
common_pitfalls: Picking a placeholder application id such as com.example.app and discovering it at upload time.
Hardcoding an SDK level from memory that Play no longer accepts.
definition_of_done: Every acceptance criterion above is demonstrably met, with evidence recorded.

checkpoint.action: Record evidence in docs/reports/STAGE_3_WORKLOG.md, then continue to substage 3.2. Do not skip ahead or work substages in parallel.
escalate_immediately_if: An open question (OQ-xx) blocks the work in front of you.

substages.name: Directory structure and layer boundaries
substages.goal: Create the exact tree from ARCHITECTURE.md and make each layer's rules visible in the filesystem.
substages.why_it_matters: Layering only holds if it is visible; a boundary nobody can see is a boundary nobody keeps.
entry_criteria: Substage 3.1 (Project initialisation and Android configuration) is complete and ticked off.

work.action: Create the directory tree exactly as specified, with no undocumented additions.
details: If you find yourself wanting a folder that is not in the design, that is a design gap - raise it and amend the document.

work.action: Add a short README.md inside each top-level layer folder.
details: What belongs here, what does not, and which direction dependencies flow.
This is read by whoever adds a file six months from now.

work.action: Create the domain layer as pure Dart with no Flutter dependency.
details: Add a placeholder type per layer so the tree is non-empty and the structure is testable.
Confirm the domain directory compiles without the Flutter SDK on the path.

work.action: Mirror the tree under test/ so a test's location is always predictable from the file it covers.
Confirm the tree against the design document line by line and record any deviation with its reason.

acceptance_criteria: The created tree matches ARCHITECTURE.md with no undocumented additions.
A search for package:flutter under the domain directory returns nothing.
Each layer folder has its README.md.
test/ mirrors lib/.
must_not: Do not add a folder that is absent from the design without amending the design.
common_pitfalls: A utils or common folder that becomes the place where layering goes to die.
definition_of_done: Every acceptance criterion above is demonstrably met, with evidence recorded.

checkpoint.action: Record evidence in docs/reports/STAGE_3_WORKLOG.md, then continue to substage 3.3. Do not skip ahead or work substages in parallel.

substages.name: Dependencies and the code generation toolchain
substages.goal: Add every dependency chosen in Stage 2, resolve current versions, and prove code generation runs end to end.
substages.why_it_matters: Dependency drift and a broken generator are the two things that silently block Stage 4.
entry_criteria: Substage 3.2 (Directory structure and layer boundaries) is complete and ticked off.

work.action: Add the packages named in the ADRs: state management, database plus its generator, Google Sign-In, the cloud client, charting, CSV, background scheduling, UUID, dependency injection, mocking, property-based testing.
details: Resolve current versions from pub.dev at this moment; do not paste versions from memory.

work.action: Re-check the minSdk floor now that plugins are present, and raise it if a plugin requires it.
details: Update docs/ENVIRONMENT.md with the plugin that sets the floor.
This is a common late-stage surprise, which is why it is re-checked here rather than assumed in 3.1.

work.action: Run the code generator once end to end against a trivial placeholder to prove the toolchain works before any real schema exists.
details: A generator that fails on the first real table in Stage 4 costs a session to diagnose.

work.action: Decide whether generated files are committed or gitignored, and apply it consistently.
Commit the lockfile so builds are reproducible.
Write docs/DEPENDENCIES.md.
details: Package, version, purpose, licence, the ADR that justified it, maintenance signal, exit plan.
Flag any dependency that is unmaintained or discontinued, and either replace it or record why it is acceptable.

work.action: Confirm no analytics, crash reporting, advertising or telemetry package has arrived transitively.
details: Inspect the resolved dependency tree, not just the direct dependencies.

acceptance_criteria: flutter pub get resolves with no version conflicts and no unexplained discontinued-package warning.
The code generation command runs successfully against a placeholder.
DEPENDENCIES.md lists every direct dependency with purpose, licence and exit plan.
The resolved tree contains no telemetry, analytics or advertising package.
The minSdk floor is re-verified against the installed plugins and recorded.
must_not: Do not add a dependency that is absent from the ADRs without recording a new one.
Do not paste a version number from memory.
common_pitfalls: Discovering in Stage 7 that the Google client raised minSdk above the level already advertised.
A generator misconfiguration that only surfaces when the first real table is written.
definition_of_done: Every acceptance criterion above is demonstrably met, with evidence recorded.

checkpoint.action: Record evidence in docs/reports/STAGE_3_WORKLOG.md, then continue to substage 3.4. Do not skip ahead or work substages in parallel.

substages.name: Linting, formatting and invariant guard checks
substages.goal: Make the manifest invariants mechanically enforceable, and prove each guard fails on a deliberate violation.
substages.why_it_matters: An invariant that nothing checks is an intention. The guards are what make INV-01 and INV-08 real for the next seven stages.
entry_criteria: Substage 3.3 (Dependencies and the code generation toolchain) is complete and ticked off.

work.action: Enable a strict analysis_options.yaml built on flutter_lints, with strict type checks and no implicit dynamic.
Implement the money-type guard.
details: Fail the build if double, float or num appears in domain or data money-path files.
A custom lint package or a scripted grep in CI both satisfy this; choose the simpler one that actually runs.

work.action: Implement the time guard: fail if DateTime.now() is called outside the Clock abstraction.
Implement the layering guard: fail if domain imports package:flutter, dart:io, or any data, application or presentation path.
Implement the telemetry guard: fail if a known analytics, crash reporting or advertising package appears in the resolved dependency tree.
Demonstrate that every guard fails on a deliberate violation, then revert each one.
details: Add a double in the domain layer, run the check, capture the failure, remove it.
Add a Flutter import in the domain layer, run the check, capture the failure, remove it.
Paste the captured failures into the stage report. A guard that has never failed has never been tested.

work.action: Configure formatting and add a format check.
Write docs/DEVELOPMENT.md covering local setup, how to run every check, how to run code generation, and the branch and commit conventions from the manifest.

acceptance_criteria: flutter analyze returns zero issues on the scaffold.
Each of the four guards has been demonstrated failing on a deliberate violation, with output captured.
The formatting check runs and passes.
DEVELOPMENT.md documents how to run every check locally.
must_not: Do not claim a guard works without demonstrating a failure.
Do not weaken a guard to make existing code pass - there is no existing code yet, so there is no excuse.
common_pitfalls: A grep-based guard with a pattern so loose it fires on comments, which then gets disabled.
Guards that only run in CI, so nobody sees them locally until the pipeline is red.
definition_of_done: Every acceptance criterion above is demonstrably met, with evidence recorded.

substages.name: Continuous integration pipeline
substages.goal: Automate the full check sequence so every later stage is verified on every push.
substages.why_it_matters: It is cheap now and it is what keeps Stages 4 through 10 honest when they get busy.
entry_criteria: Substage 3.4 (Linting, formatting and invariant guard checks) is complete and ticked off.

work.action: Create a workflow that runs on every push: pub get, format check, analyze, all four guards, unit tests, and a debug build.
Cache pub and Gradle directories so the pipeline stays fast enough that people wait for it.
Fail the pipeline on any analyzer issue, not only on errors.
Add a coverage report step now, while coverage is near zero, so the trend is visible from the first commit.
Verify the pipeline runs green on the scaffold commit, and capture the run output.
Deliberately break formatting, confirm the pipeline goes red, then revert.
If no CI host is available, provide the identical sequence as a single local check script and say so explicitly in the stage report.
details: The requirement is that one command runs every check, not that a particular host runs it.

acceptance_criteria: The pipeline, or the equivalent single local command, runs every check in one invocation.
It runs green on the scaffold commit, with output captured.
A deliberate formatting break turns it red, demonstrated and reverted.
A coverage figure is produced, even though it is near zero.
outputs: CI workflow file or check script.
must_not: Do not let the pipeline pass while the analyzer reports issues.
common_pitfalls: A pipeline so slow that it gets bypassed.
Coverage reporting added later, so no trend exists when it matters.
definition_of_done: Every acceptance criterion above is demonstrably met, with evidence recorded.

substages.name: Theme, design tokens and the money formatter
substages.goal: Define light and dark themes, spacing and typography tokens, the business scope treatment, and a correct currency formatter.
substages.why_it_matters: Doing this once now is far cheaper than restyling twenty finished screens in Stage 10, and the formatter is on the money path.
entry_criteria: Substage 3.5 (Continuous integration pipeline) is complete and ticked off.

work.action: Define the colour scheme, typography scale and spacing tokens in one place, for both light and dark.
Define the business scope's visual treatment as a theme extension rather than scattered colour literals.
details: It must not rely on colour alone, because NFR-08 requires meaning to survive greyscale.

work.action: Implement the currency formatter.
details: Reads the configured ISO 4217 code and minor unit exponent from settings.
Handles exponent 0 such as JPY, exponent 2 such as USD and PKR, and exponent 3 such as KWD.
Formats from an integer minor-unit value and never accepts or produces a floating point number.
Handles negative amounts and very large amounts without overflow or truncation.
Applies locale-appropriate grouping separators.

work.action: Implement the shared presentation primitives Stage 6 will need, with no logic in them.
details: Money text display, progress-toward-ceiling indicator, empty state, error state, loading state.

work.action: Write widget tests for the money formatter now.
details: Exponent 0, 2 and 3; zero; one minor unit; negative; a value near the documented maximum; and a locale with a different grouping separator.

work.action: Verify every stub screen renders legibly in dark mode.

acceptance_criteria: No colour, spacing or font literal appears outside the theme definition.
Money formatter tests pass, covering exponents 0, 2 and 3, negatives, and extreme values.
The formatter has no code path that accepts or returns a floating point number.
The business scope treatment is legible in greyscale.
Dark mode renders every stub without unreadable text.
must_not: Do not hardcode two decimal places anywhere.
Do not put any computation in the money text widget - it formats, it does not calculate.
common_pitfalls: A formatter that divides by 100 in a double, reintroducing floating point on the display path.
A business colour that becomes invisible in dark mode.
definition_of_done: Every acceptance criterion above is demonstrably met, with evidence recorded.

substages.name: Router and stub screens
substages.goal: Implement the navigation graph from NAVIGATION.md with one placeholder screen per route.
substages.why_it_matters: Stage 6 should be filling prepared rooms, not deciding where the walls go.
entry_criteria: Substage 3.6 (Theme, design tokens and the money formatter) is complete and ticked off.
inputs: ADR-001 for how navigation state is held.

work.action: Implement the router chosen in Stage 2, with a route for every screen in the inventory.
Create one stub widget per screen containing only its title and an explicit placeholder marker.
details: No logic, no data, and nothing that could be mistaken for working functionality.
The placeholder should visibly say it is a placeholder.

work.action: Wire the bottom navigation or scope switch that separates personal and business, per the Stage 2 decision.
details: Include the personal-only case: no business surface at all.

work.action: Implement Android back behaviour for every multi-step flow as designed, including the onboarding step chain.
Add a temporary developer route menu listing every route so a reviewer can reach each stub in one tap.
details: Mark it clearly for removal in Stage 10, and add it to the Stage 10 checklist now rather than trusting memory.

work.action: Walk every route manually and confirm reachability, then record the walk in the stage report.

acceptance_criteria: Every route in NAVIGATION.md is reachable from the running app.
There is no dead route and no route that is absent from the design document.
Placeholders visibly identify themselves as placeholders.
Android back behaviour matches the design for every multi-step flow.
The developer menu is present and is already listed on the Stage 10 removal checklist.
must_not: Do not add fake data to a stub.
Do not create a route that the design does not contain.
common_pitfalls: A developer menu that survives to release because nobody wrote it down.
Stubs with realistic dummy figures that get screenshotted as progress.
definition_of_done: Every acceptance criterion above is demonstrably met, with evidence recorded.

substages.name: Test harness, fakes and fixtures
substages.goal: Build the testing foundations Stages 4 and 5 depend on, and prove they work.
substages.why_it_matters: Stages 4 and 5 are test-first. A harness invented under pressure is a harness that shapes tests around convenience.
entry_criteria: Substage 3.7 (Router and stub screens) is complete and ticked off.

work.action: Create the test directory structure mirroring lib/.
Implement a fake Clock that returns a fixed or scripted time, so no test depends on wall-clock time.
Implement a deterministic IdGenerator that produces predictable ids, so expected outputs are stable across runs.
Implement test data builders for the domain entities, with sensible defaults and named overrides.
details: A builder pattern keeps tests readable when an entity gains a field in Stage 4.

work.action: Implement the golden vector loader that reads JSON fixtures from a directory and yields cases.
details: Stage 5 depends on this; adding a fixture must require no code change.

work.action: Add one trivial passing test per layer that actually uses the fake Clock and the deterministic IdGenerator.
details: A fake nobody exercises is a fake nobody has tested.

work.action: Configure integration_test and verify with one trivial app-launch test on a device or emulator.
Confirm the whole suite runs from the single CI command created in substage 3.5.

acceptance_criteria: flutter test passes.
flutter test integration_test launches the app and passes on a device or emulator.
The fake Clock and deterministic IdGenerator are exercised by the trivial tests.
The golden vector loader reads a sample fixture with no code change required to add another.
The full suite runs from the single CI command.
outputs: Fakes, builders and the fixture loader.
must_not: Do not write a test that reads the system clock.
common_pitfalls: A fixture loader hardcoded to a list of filenames, which then requires a code change per vector in Stage 5.
definition_of_done: Every acceptance criterion above is demonstrably met, with evidence recorded.

substages.name: Scaffold verification and gate preparation
substages.goal: Prove the scaffold matches the design, capture the evidence, and prepare the stage gate.
substages.why_it_matters: This is the contract check the whole stage exists for.
entry_criteria: Substage 3.8 (Test harness, fakes and fixtures) is complete and ticked off.

work.action: Produce a design-versus-implementation comparison for the directory tree, route list and dependency list.
details: Three tables, each with a design column, an implemented column and a difference column.
A non-empty difference column requires either a fix or a documented, justified deviation.

work.action: Run the full check command from a clean checkout and capture the output.
details: Clean checkout matters: it catches anything that only works because of local state.

work.action: Build and run on a physical device, walk every route, and confirm dark mode and 200 percent font scale do not break any stub.
Confirm the project contains no business logic, no persistence and no network code, by inspection and by search.
Record every version actually used in docs/ENVIRONMENT.md, superseding any provisional entry.
Write docs/reports/STAGE_3_REPORT.md with the comparison tables, the guard failure demonstrations, the CI output and the route walk.
Update docs/TRACEABILITY.md where a requirement's implementing artefact now exists.
Prepare the gate question, listing versions used and any deviation from the design.

acceptance_criteria: All three comparison tables show either no differences or documented, justified deviations.
The full check command passes from a clean checkout, with output captured.
Every route was walked on a physical device and no stub breaks in dark mode or at 200 percent font scale.
A search confirms no business logic, persistence or network code exists.
The stage report contains the guard failure demonstrations from substage 3.4.
must_not: Do not proceed to Stage 4 with an undocumented deviation from the approved design.
common_pitfalls: Verifying from a working tree that has local files the repository does not contain.
Reporting the scaffold complete without walking the routes on a real device.
definition_of_done: Every acceptance criterion above is demonstrably met, with evidence recorded.

checkpoint.action: Final substage. Assemble the stage report, then STOP and request approval using approval_gate.question_to_user below.
escalate_immediately_if: A deviation from the design that you believe is correct - amend the design document and raise it rather than diverging silently.

stage_deliverables.path: CI workflow or equivalent check script

stage_definition_of_done: The app builds and launches on a real device or emulator.
Every screen from NAVIGATION.md exists as a reachable stub.
flutter analyze is clean and every guard check demonstrably fails on a deliberate violation.
CI or the equivalent local script runs green and its output is pasted into the stage report.
No business logic, no database and no network code exists anywhere in the project.
stage_must_not: Do not implement real data persistence, not even a temporary in-memory store.
Do not implement any business logic, including a quick percentage calculation.
Do not populate stub screens with hardcoded data that looks real.
Do not wire Google Sign-In or request any OAuth scope in this stage.
Do not deviate from the approved directory structure without amending ARCHITECTURE.md and saying so.
anti_patterns: A scaffold that quietly diverges from the architecture doc, so the doc is wrong from day one.
Stub screens with plausible dummy numbers that get demoed as progress.
Skipping the lint guards because we will be careful - the guards are what make INV-01 real.

artifacts_next_stage_consumes: Data layer folders and the code-generation toolchain are ready for Stage 4.
The test harness, fake Clock and deterministic IdGenerator are ready for Stages 4 and 5.
Stub screens are ready for Stage 6.
The theme and money formatter are ready for every UI stage.
handoff.summary_to_write: Record exact versions used and every place the scaffold had to deviate from the design, with the reason.

approval_gate.question_to_user: Stage 3 (Scaffolding) is complete. The app builds and every designed screen is reachable as a stub. Versions used: <list>. Deviations from the design: <list or none>. Do you approve moving to Stage 4?
